# moddotplot-rs v0.2.0-beta.1

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

This is the first hardened beta of the browser-native rewrite. It is a functional
preview for scientific evaluation, not yet a research-validated release. This release
cycle produced local artifacts only; nothing was deployed, uploaded, or published.

## Highlights

* Entirely client-side FASTA and gzip FASTA processing in Rust/WebAssembly.
* Independent X/Y record selection for self and pairwise comparisons.
* Verified-winner OPH containment estimation with ntHash2 and HLL p10.
* A 256-register quick view followed by streamed 1,024-register refinement.
* Detailed tiles replace quick tiles individually as compatible blocks finish.
* Responsive WebGL2 similarity/orientation rendering with bounded caches, progressive
  zoom detail, and exact canonical k-mer terminal zoom.
* Transactional sequence loading, stale-work cancellation, worker restart/reload,
  context restoration, and pre-allocation memory admission.
* BED/GFF/GTF import and feature tracks have been removed. The experiment remains
  recoverable from Git tag `v0.1.0`, but it did not meet this beta's reliability bar.

## Release evidence

The [validation record](v0.2.0-beta.1/VALIDATION.md) records the source commit,
commands, environment, complete test matrix, statistical report, full-chromosome
performance results, cache trace, and known validation boundaries. Machine-readable
results are stored beside it.

On an Apple M5 Pro MacBook Pro in Google Chrome 152, CHM13 chromosome 1 produced its
first preview tile 0.83 seconds after sequence parsing completed, a coherent preview
at 4.78 seconds from input selection, and a stable refined viewport at 7.59 seconds.
The CHM13/HG002 paternal chromosome 1 comparison produced its first pairwise tile in
0.60 seconds, a coherent preview in 5.47 seconds, and a stable refined viewport in
11.15 seconds after axis selection. These are machine-specific measurements, not
performance guarantees.

## Known limitations

* The one-billion-base record limit is an input upper bound, not a laptop performance
  guarantee. Sequence/sketch sharding and optional bounded disk spill are not present.
* Approximate k-mer identity below roughly 80% is outside the target operating regime.
* High-sensitivity sparse correction is optional and can increase memory substantially.
* Session persistence and numeric/high-resolution image export are not implemented.
* Automated behavioral coverage spans Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, and installed Chrome.
  Stable numeric/pixel goldens and a broader biological validation grid remain open.
* Actual Safari WebDriver testing requires the user's disabled global “Allow remote
  automation” setting; the release process did not modify it. WebKit 26.5 was tested.
* Static files require HTTP or HTTPS. Direct `file://` execution is unsupported.

## Local artifacts

The release tool creates separate source and deployable-web archives, SHA-256 sums,
and build provenance under ignored `release-artifacts/`. The web archive includes the
license, citation metadata, SBOM, dependency licenses, notices, user/scientific docs,
and static assets. No artifact is transmitted by the tool.
